strips.hook: [device: ritual-as-agency] [target: the protagonists' own failings | form: two-hander | aim: inward | mechanic: anti-work-equilibrium | cast: Milo+Cal] You refresh the inbox that would have pinged you anyway - not for the reply, for the one thing at work that responds the second you ask. (2-panel recut: the 3-panel original was killed under S13, user 2026-08-02 - the reveal closed in panel 2 and panel 3 topped it.)
strips.caption: The button is the only one that answers.

strips.hook: [device: maintained-incompetence] [target: cross-functional friction | form: two-hander | aim: lateral | mechanic: anti-work-equilibrium | cast: Cal+Susie] Cal has forwarded the same customer security question to the solutions engineer eleven times and blocks Susie from explaining it in four sentences — because being unable to answer is exactly what keeps Ravi on his calls. Seeded by the relatability radar (Reddit unreachable): HN 465up/379c 'Prevent cognitive debt by manually retyping LLM-generated code' and Lobsters 96up 'Don't be a meat proxy' — two threads full of the same confessed behavior, shipping expert output you never understood. Works with all news deleted.
strips.caption:
The fastest answer in the building was written by somebody else.

Everybody has pasted an expert's reply to a customer without reading it twice. A few people have quietly decided that's the entire job — and they are not wrong about how deals get signed.

strips.hook: [device: engineered-error] [target: cross-functional friction | form: two-hander | aim: lateral | mechanic: perverse-incentive-harvest | cast: Susie+Maren] Marketing catches a wrong stat in Susie's follow-up to a silent prospect. The error is the instrument: a prospect who can ignore a question cannot ignore a mistake, so every email she sends has exactly one number wrong.
strips.caption:
You cannot make a prospect answer you. You can make them correct you.

Susie's follow-ups all have exactly one thing wrong with them. Marketing found out this morning.

strips.hook: [device: process-recursion] [target: bureaucratic process | form: two-hander | aim: systemic | mechanic: policy-as-punchline | cast: Milo+Frank] The cheap purchase is the slow one — the fix is to spend more. Standalone; references nothing outside its own three panels. Scored 29/30 by independent craft judges in two separate rounds and passed the cold-scroller gate in both.

[device: compliance-laundering] [target: vendors & procurement | form: two-hander | aim: outward | mechanic: weaponised-literalism | cast: Frank+Susie] Susie needs a $1,240 tool only one vendor makes. The three-quote rule looks unsatisfiable without lying — so Frank, who enforces it, tells her to ask the vendor she already chose for its own competitor sheet: two real names, priced to lose.

[device: loophole-as-deliverable] [target: cross-functional friction | form: two-hander, peer request-and-supply (no authority, no newcomer) | aim: lateral | mechanic: loophole-as-deliverable — a legitimate deliverable's real specification IS the loophole, disclosed plainly by the person who built it | cast: Cal + Maren (Maren's first appearance of the run)] Cal owes a stalled prospect a touch and has nothing to say, so he shops Marketing for something the prospect can't ghost; Maren hands him the working exploit — page one is the argument, the other eight pages make it a favour instead of a question.

[device: mandated-honesty-relocates] [target: bureaucratic process | form: two-hander (no protagonist — Cal and HOBS absent) | aim: systemic | mechanic: the-wrong-lesson | cast: Diane + Susie] Susie keeps a private sheet of the four deals that are actually real, outside a nineteen-deal CRM. Diane loves the honesty and mandates one from every rep by Friday. Susie complies and opens a new private sheet: nineteen go in yours, four in mine. Radar seed: HN 'Developers are attached to tools because tools encode trust' (224 up / 124 comments) plus the Lobsters 'Controlling Your Environment Makes You Happy' revival — both threads are full of the confessed behaviour of trusting your own instrument over the mandated one. News-independent by construction.
strips.caption:
Everyone has a second spreadsheet.

The one the CRM doesn't know about — the four deals that are actually real. It stays honest for exactly as long as nobody asks for it.

strips.hook: [device: proxy-metric-harvest] [target: metrics gaming | form: two-hander | aim: upward | mechanic: perverse-incentive harvest | cast: Diane + Cal] A VP puts a one-hour reply SLA on her dashboard; Cal promises nine minutes, because the dashboard times the FIRST reply and nothing has ever timed the second one. Seeded by the relatability radar (HN 2026-08-03, 'Don't be a meat proxy', 330 up / 143 comments — the confessed behaviour of relaying instantly while adding nothing) and by SaaStr's '10x times zero is still zero' line on speed without substance. Works with all news deleted.
